- **claim-fixed-tuple-exclusion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-indices-fixed-exclusion)): With the preceding cap choices, a fixed-type tuple satisfying properties (i) and (ii) of Definition <a href="#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:indices:analytic-hypotheses">80</a> has no true $J$-cut. No mixed projection regularity is assumed in this assertion. It is a single type $A$ component with no lens end, particles, or other positive loss. Its cut-down instanton dimension is zero.
  - Explanation: The virtual score identity excludes fixed-type cuts and losses, leaving only an unbroken isolated irreducible instanton.
- **claim-reducible-run-projection-score** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-indices-mixed-run)): For a nonempty contiguous run of $r$ interior components of type $R$, $$\label{eq:indices:mixed-run} \sum_{i\text{ in the run}}(4+i_i-p_i)\ge-2.$$ More precisely, let $s,m$ be the total assigned tests and positive cells, let $s_P$ count occupied positive-cell slots, and let $\mathrm{miss}=2m-s_P$. With $\Delta$ the telescoping endpoint bit difference, $$\label{eq:indices:mixed-run-sharp} \sum(4+i_i-p_i) \ge s-4m+r+\Delta+3\,\mathrm{miss}.$$
  - Explanation: Missing positive-cell slots strengthen the reducible-run bound needed after discarding zero-spinor reducers.
- **claim-mixed-tuple-exclusion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-indices-mixed-exclusion)): A tuple containing type $P$, satisfying the type $R$ incidence in property (ii) and the projection property (iii) of Definition <a href="#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:indices:analytic-hypotheses">80</a>, has no true $J$-cut. It has no particles or other integer losses. Apart from an unbroken free main field, the only possible case is one separated lens end of effective trace charge $1/4$, a single main component of type $P$, and no other lens end or loss.
  - Explanation: The necessary projected dimension excludes true primary cuts and integer losses, leaving only the clean free field or a single minimum trace lens end.
- **claim-numerical-boundary-exclusion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-thm-indices-exclusion)): Choose the old-cap data, outside delays, exceptional evaluations, finite stack, metric sizes, and sufficiently small equation data in the order of Lemma <a href="#lem:indices:end-exclusion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:indices:end-exclusion">85</a> and Corollary <a href="#cor:estimates:choices" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:estimates:choices">73</a>, with $n_D^{\rm tot}>0$. Assume the regularity, incidence, and projection properties of Definition <a href="#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:indices:analytic-hypotheses">80</a>. Then the only fixed-type tuples meeting the nonphase cuts are the legitimate unbroken isolated type $A$ instantons. The free part after the $\eta=n_D^{\rm tot}-1$ phase cuts and phase quotient has expected dimension one. Its only possible true-face or positive-loss limiting tuples are single trace-minimum lens faces, with one type $P$ main component and no other losses. Consequently the only boundary types to be constructed for its compactified one-dimensional count are links of the legitimate instantons and those trace-minimum ends.
  - Explanation: With the analytic admissibility properties, only legitimate instanton links and loss-free minimum trace lens ends can bound the free spinor count.
- **claim-compatible-regularization** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-analysis-regularization)): For the fixed finite family, equation perturbations and representatives can be chosen arbitrarily small in the prescribed norms with the following properties.* 1. *Ordinary irreducible equations and the labelled sphere, surface, and point tests are transverse, including the relevant ideal and broken strata. Their representatives have the exact support and persistence properties of Lemma <a href="#lem:analysis:incidence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:analysis:incidence">99</a>. They are compatible with fixed determinant gluing, marked translation on cylinders, and all true faces. Prescribed harmonic reducers on separated caps are preserved.* 2. *Single-component, single-valued equivariant perturbations give the fixed-type regularity in Definition <a href="#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:indices:analytic-hypotheses">80</a>. Every tuple of fixed type is consequently excluded except the legitimate unbroken cut-down instantons.* 3. *A finite collection of rational multisection terms, in addition to single-valued terms, eliminates every forbidden mixed ideal stratum by the negative dimension of its necessary projection. No equation or retained cut on this projection depends on discarded $R$ fields or their particles. The allowed free stratum is regular of dimension one, and the single trace-end main problem is regular of dimension zero. Choices on the exterior of a separated lens cap agree under the corresponding bit flip.* 4. *Solutions have the compactness, removable-singularity, integral particle-charge, and exponential true-end properties proved below. Near each legitimate instanton, the phase-cut link has oriented count $2^\eta$ times its instanton sign, where $\eta=n_D^{\rm tot}-1$.* *The finite branch lists have compatible weighted germs and total weight one. After the no-particle end gluing of Section <a href="#sec:gluing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gluing">10</a>, their oriented one-dimensional zero sets obey the ordinary rational Stokes rule.
  - Explanation: Small compatible perturbations supply ordinary and fixed-type regularity, exclude forbidden mixed candidates, and produce oriented instanton links and weighted boundary counts.
- **claim-zero-winding-modification** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-zero-winding)): Fix $1/2<b<1$. On the Hilbert manifold of $H^b$ paths $g:[0,1]\longrightarrow\operatorname{SU}(2)$ with endpoints $1$ there is a smooth conjugation-equivariant operation $g\mapsto\widehat g$, homotopic to the identity operation relative to the endpoints, such that every commuting path of winding zero has image a uniform positive distance from $-1$. The operation fixes commuting paths of nonzero winding. It uses only the given path.
  - Explanation: A smooth equivariant path operation moves commuting zero-winding paths uniformly away from the incidence target and fixes nonzero-winding commuting paths.
- **claim-primary-test-segmentation** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-segmentation)): The sphere representatives can be chosen so that, at a true $J$ face, their event is the disjoint union of the events on the two half spheres, with the prescribed signs. During the change from the whole-sphere rule to this rule, a commuting path whose two half degrees vanish retains a uniform avoidance gap. Every event on the face is intrinsic to its assigned side; no derivative of transport along the growing neck enters its definition.
  - Explanation: Primary-face events split into intrinsic half-sphere events while preserving avoidance when both half evaluations vanish.
- **claim-finite-framed-samples** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-samples)): Finite framed samples, avoiding any specified finite particle set, detect the stabilizer of a smooth field. They give arbitrary curvature and retained cut variations at type $A$, and arbitrary tangential curvature and active-line spinor variations at type $S$. With a type $P$ witness they give arbitrary full equation and retained cut variations at every non-$R$ target, using finite weighted branch lists if needed. Phase-cut values can be varied using the witness alone.
  - Explanation: Finite samples detect stabilizers and provide the allowed tangential or full variation directions, with finite branch lists at mixed targets.
- **claim-independent-ordinary-library** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-analysis-ordinary-library)): The preceding construction at zero spinor supplies the ordinary representatives and perturbations used in Sections <a href="#sec:ordinary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:ordinary">2</a> and <a href="#sec:caps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:caps">4</a>. It is independent of the existence or value of the closed cap count. It permits simultaneous regularity on the countably many required lower strata and normal derivative regularization at the specified harmonic reducers while fixing their values.
  - Explanation: The ordinary exact-support library is available independently of cap nonvanishing and preserves harmonic reducer values while regularizing their normal derivatives.
- **claim-discarded-field-independence** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-r-independence)): The coupled terms can be supported so that they vanish on every tuple of fixed type. On an exact $J$ face a term involving a connected graph in an $R$ component vanishes on a neighborhood of that sample. After discarding $R$ fields, their particles, and their tests, every remaining equation and cut is a function only of the retained fields and particles and of the retained parameter variables. The same assertion holds for separated lens-cap data.
  - Explanation: Support restrictions remove all dependence on discarded reducers and their atoms, including dependence hidden in energy cutoffs.
- **claim-compatible-implicit-charts** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-scale)): Let $E_s=c^{a+s,\alpha}_\delta$ and $F_s=c^{a+s-1,\alpha}_\delta$, with the finite-dimensional equation, parameter, and cut variables included. For the sampling formulas above, the equation map at level $s$ is $C^1$. For every prescribed $j$ it is $C^j$ from sufficiently high field order to $F_s$. At a smooth universally surjective zero its universal solution set has $C^j$ local charts, for every prescribed finite $j$, with the same perturbation space $\mathfrak P$ and the same smooth finite-dimensional kernel coordinates at all levels.
  - Explanation: Increasing field regularity supplies the differentiability required for compatible finite-order implicit charts, without assuming unlimited same-order path differentiation.
- **claim-body-compactness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-compactness)): For the fixed finite family, and for perturbations in a sufficiently small bounded set of the norms above, the following statements hold uniformly, including coefficient-convergent sequences of already ideal solutions.* 1. *The trace-free curvature and covariant spinor gradient are bounded in $L^2$, and the spinor is bounded in $L^4$.* 2. *The measure $\|\Phi\|^4\,d\operatorname{Vol}$ has no atoms in a weak limit, including a limit obtained by translating along a true cylinder. Neither does $\|F_a^{0,+}\|^2\,d\operatorname{Vol}$.* 3. *On compact sets, a subsequence converges modulo gauge away from finitely many points. The limiting field extends across these points and solves the same equations with the ideal cutoff formula <a href="#eq:analysis:energy-cutoff" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:analysis:energy-cutoff">[eq:analysis:energy-cutoff]</a>. The lost charges are positive integers, and each charge-$m$ atom has mass $8\pi^2m$ in the stated curvature norm.* 4. *On any fixed ideal stratum, if there is no further bubbling or end loss, convergence is in the completed higher-order field charts. At a new bubble there is still convergence in $C^{0,\beta}$ on surviving exact cut paths for any fixed $\beta<1$.
  - Explanation: Energy bounds, nonconcentration, removable singularities, and charge quantization give ideal compactness and the stated surviving-path convergence.
- **claim-true-neck-completion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-neck)): Along a sequence in which genuine neck lengths tend to infinity, a subsequence has finitely many particles and nonconstant cylinder levels. Every translated cylinder level has zero spinor and is ASD. Nonconstant levels have a discrete positive charge cost. The remaining necks carry no diffuse loss and converge to matching flat states with exponential decay of all derivatives. On a no-loss stretch of length $T$ the deviation from the flat orbit is bounded by exponentially decreasing contributions from its two ends and from the prescribed forcing.
  - Explanation: A finite extraction of positive-charge ASD levels and particles leaves flat matching necks with exponential decay and no diffuse energy loss.
- **claim-exact-support-incidence** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-incidence)): At an ideal limit a basic sphere, surface, or point test persists unless a particle meets its exact basic support. In that case one may drop the test with its auxiliary evaluation variable, while retaining the particle’s incidence with that support. For every particle of weight $m$, the dimension of its permitted position plus the degrees released by all such dropped tests is at most $4m$. The zero-evaluation sphere rules in Definition <a href="#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:indices:analytic-hypotheses">80</a> hold, with different charged tests using distinct loss units.
  - Explanation: Tests persist away from exact support hits. Position and released-degree budgets preserve strict loss penalties and prevent charging the same loss unit twice.
- **claim-finite-degeneration-data** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-finite-data)): For this finite problem the degeneration data needed for candidate exclusion have finite ranges. Order the data by: deeper true faces; larger total effective end and particle loss; fewer distinct main particle locations at fixed loss; more dropped tests; and more $R$ components. Treat finite assignment, closed support-stratum, and rank choices together at each step. In a fixed finite branch library, if the single-valued coefficients converge in $\mathfrak P$ and the additional finite coefficients converge, every sequence of candidates has a subsequence which either converges modulo the completed field slices at the same step or limits to an earlier step or a fixed-type tuple.
  - Explanation: Bounded discrete losses and splitting classes give a finite degeneration ordering; candidate sequences either remain compact at their step or degenerate earlier.
- **claim-fixed-stage-regularity** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-analysis-first-stage)): There is an arbitrarily small single-valued, single-component choice for which type $A$ equations with all retained nonphase tests are transverse on every relevant ideal and parameter stratum, and type $S$ tangential equations are transverse. The first two conditions of Definition <a href="#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:indices:analytic-hypotheses">80</a> follow. The only fixed-type tuples are a finite set of legitimate unbroken cut-down instantons, and the coupled complex Dirac operator can also be made surjective at each of them without altering the instanton equations.
  - Explanation: Single-component regularization proves fixed-type admissibility and leaves finitely many legitimate instantons whose Dirac operators can be made surjective without moving the ordinary equations.
- **claim-instanton-link-degree** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-analysis-instanton-link)): Put $n_*=n_D^{\rm tot}>0$ and $\eta=n_*-1$. At each legitimate cut-down instanton, the normal spinor link before phase quotient is $S^{2n_*-1}/\{\pm1\}$ and its phase quotient is $\mathbb{CP}^{n_*-1}$. The phase-character-two line restricts to $\mathcal O(2)$ on this projective space. The $\eta$ phase sections can be chosen so that their cut-down link is regular and has signed count $$\label{eq:analysis:instanton-degree} 2^\eta\,\operatorname{sign}(a).$$ There is one fixed overall boundary-orientation convention in this formula, the same for every instanton. Subsequent mixed branch terms may be kept zero near these links.
  - Explanation: The center quotient and original phase character determine the projective normal link and doubled hyperplane cuts, preserving the ordinary instanton sign.
- **claim-necessary-mixed-projection** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-projection)): For a candidate containing a $P$ field, delete the $R$ fields, their particle positions, and their tests, but retain their parameter variables. Quotient the remaining fields by their independent gauges and the common phase. This defines a Fredholm problem with finite isotropy near its candidate projections. Its dimension, before phase quotient and phase cuts, is at most $$\label{eq:analysis:projected-dimension} \sum_{i\notin R}\left( i_i-\sum_{\text{lens ends of }i}(\delta_{\rm sp}-1)-2w_i\right) +\sum_{i\in R}p_i.$$ The phase cuts and quotient subtract $2\eta+1$. At every such candidate projection, admissible local finite-branch variations make the universal equations and retained cuts transverse.
  - Explanation: Discarding reducer fields while keeping their parameters yields a finite-isotropy Fredholm problem with the stated conservative dimension bound and available local variations.
- **claim-finite-mixed-exclusion** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-analysis-finite-induction)): After the first-stage choices, finitely many additional local multisection terms with arbitrarily small coefficients exclude all forbidden mixed candidates. The only remaining mixed candidate types are the unbroken free part and the single trace-minimum lens-end main problem of Proposition <a href="#prop:indices:mixed-exclusion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:indices:mixed-exclusion">88</a>. The latter is regular of dimension zero. The unbroken free problem has expected dimension one; its regularization follows the lens gluing in Section <a href="#sec:gluing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gluing">10</a>. The additional choices agree on paired lens exteriors and are zero near the legitimate instanton collars.
  - Explanation: Finite local multisection additions eliminate negative-index candidate projections and regularize the remaining minimum trace-main problems relative to protected instanton collars.
- **claim-weighted-boundary-rule** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-analysis-stokes)): A compact oriented one-dimensional zero set built from the finite branch lists above in the surviving free stratum has total weighted oriented boundary zero. Its weights are rational, and a region on which every additional branch term is zero has the weight of the original single-valued problem.
  - Explanation: Compatible oriented finite branch germs obey the rational boundary rule and retain the original weight wherever added terms vanish.
- **claim-regular-minimum-trace-cap** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-gluing-regular-cap)): At each of finitely many regular isolated main-component limits on a trace face, the cap data can be chosen arbitrarily small, compatibly with the preceding exclusions, so that the following statements hold. The framed cap problem of charge $1/4$, with its sphere-sweep mark and the normalized holonomy condition $-1$, is a finite set of regular points. Every point is a crossing on the unique harmonic Abelian connection with ordered summand difference $v(S)=2$. These points are fixed by $H$, and their oriented sum has absolute value one. The spinor is zero, and the coupled Dirac operator is invertible at each point. The choices for the two determinant lifts are related by the prescribed cap tensor operation.
  - Explanation: Small cap adjustments make minimum-charge harmonic crossings framed regular points with invertible Dirac operators and tensor-paired lift data.
- **claim-augmented-weight-blocks** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-gluing-blocks)): After fixing phase as above, the positive-weight main augmented constrained operator $L_M^+$ is an isomorphism. On the cap the positive-weight augmented constrained operator $L_N^+$ has zero kernel and has precisely the one-dimensional cokernel $$\ell(f)=\int_N\langle\tau,f_{\mathrm{gauge}}\rangle. \label{eq:gluing:scalar-cokernel}$$ Here $f_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ is its $G^*$-component and $\tau$ is the parallel diagonal gauge generator on the cap. Changing the cap field weight from $+\delta$ to $-\delta$ gives an isomorphism $L_N^-$.
  - Explanation: The phase-fixed main block is invertible. The cap has precisely the parallel scalar obstruction at positive weight, removed by the specified weight change.
- **claim-triangular-parameter-elimination** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-gluing-triangular)): Let $p$ denote the main parameter and auxiliary-variable directions which also occur in the cap equations or cap cut. Locally the limiting representative $\gamma$, collar gauges, and link metric can be kept fixed. In these choices, the limiting coupled derivative can be reduced to $L_M^+\oplus L_N^-$ by a triangular change of variables. The field part of its cap correction to $p$ decays exponentially.
  - Explanation: A decaying cap correction absorbs derivatives of shared parameters and reduces the limiting derivative to the independent weighted blocks.
- **claim-regular-lens-collars** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-gluing-collar)): For every matching pair $(u_M,u_N)$ above and every sufficiently large finite lens-neck length $D$, there is exactly one nearby unbroken zero in a fixed local branch, modulo determinant-one gauge and effective phase. These zeros depend continuously, and smoothly in finite-order solution charts, on $D$. Every sequence of unbroken zeros converging to this pair belongs to this collar for all sufficiently large lengths. The construction preserves the finite branch lists, their multiplicities, and their weights.
  - Explanation: An asymmetric-weight inverse and contraction argument construct unique lens collars and exhaust converging zeros while preserving branch multiplicities and weights.
- **claim-spinor-lens-sign-cancellation** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-gluing-signs)): For every regular trace-face main solution and every local branch, the two caps obtained by flipping its lens bit have opposite oriented contributions after multiplication by $\varepsilon(\mathbf e)$. This comparison is independent of the main solution, respects all remaining gluings, and preserves the branch weights. In particular it is the relative sign of Proposition <a href="#prop:negative:local-sign" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:negative:local-sign">25</a>, with no new sign choice.
  - Explanation: The ordinary local cap comparison extends through the complex Dirac orientation and pairs every weighted spinor lens contribution with its opposite.
- **claim-boundary-count-contradiction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-thm-gluing-contradiction)): The finite stack of Theorem <a href="#thm:stack:nonzero" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:stack:nonzero">53</a> cannot exist under an orientation-preserving identification $Y_{-2}\cong Y_2$. Consequently the remaining oriented cosmetic pair of slopes $-2$ and $2$ is impossible.
  - Explanation: Exhaustive compactification and paired lens cancellation force the nonzero instanton-link contribution to vanish, contradicting the assumed cosmetic identification.

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-ordinary-polygon",
        "exact_quote": "A path of adjacent slopes has a smooth toric local model over a polygon. Choose clockwise primitive slope vectors $w_0,\\ldots,w_m$ with $\\det(w_i,w_{i+1})=-1$. Collapse the circle of slope $w_i$ over the corresponding side and the whole torus at each corner, and attach the remaining boundary to the knot exterior times an interval. An arc from the exterior boundary to side $i$ gives the primary cut $Z_i=Y_{w_i}$. An arc between sides $i,j$, $j-i\\ge2$, gives a cut $M_{ij}$ bounding the linear plumbing associated with the intervening sides. Its spheres have consecutive intersections $+1$ and squares $-d_k$, where $$\\label{eq:ordinary:fan-relation}\n w_{k-1}+w_{k+1}=d_kw_k.$$ If the two endpoint slopes agree, the plumbing boundary is $L=S^1\\times S^2$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-ordinary-perturbations",
        "exact_quote": "For the finite ordinary families used in this section one can choose arbitrarily small compatible perturbations with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *Irreducible equations, together with any specified finite collection of auxiliary evaluations, are transverse, using variations supported in the same component. On a split face, variations on different components are independent.*\n\n2.  *At a specified harmonic reducible, perturbations can vanish in value while prescribing arbitrary finite-rank complex-linear maps from the off-diagonal kernel to the off-diagonal cokernel. Thus a complex index-zero normal operator can be made invertible, and a complex index-one normal operator can be made surjective.*\n\n3.  *Evaluation of an irreducible field at an $S^1\\times S^2$ end is transverse to a local flat slice. Fixing a central flat imposes three real conditions in that slice.*\n\n*The equation perturbations are independent of auxiliary cut marks.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-ordinary-neck-decay",
        "exact_quote": "Give $L=S^1\\times S^2$ the product metric, and let $\\alpha$ be a flat connection with parallel stabilizer $H$. On a sufficiently small-energy neck, modulo gauge, the spatial field has the form $$\\label{eq:ordinary:harmonic-slice}\n a(t)=\\alpha+h(t)\\vartheta+b(t),\n \\quad h(t)\\in H^0_\\alpha(L;\\operatorname{ad}),\n \\quad b(t)\\perp H^1_\\alpha(L;\\operatorname{ad}),\n \\quad d_\\alpha^*b(t)=0.$$ Here $\\vartheta$ is the circle one-form and the temporal component has zero parallel part. For $[-T,T]$ and any sufficiently small fixed decay rate $\\delta>0$, the normal part satisfies estimates of the form $$\\label{eq:ordinary:normal-decay}\n \\|b(t)\\|_{k}\n \\le C_k\\bigl(B_-e^{-\\delta(t+T)}\n                  +B_+e^{-\\delta(T-t)}\\bigr)\n       +C_k\\int_{-T}^T e^{-\\delta|t-s|}\\rho_k(s)\\,ds,$$ where $B_\\pm$ measure the end-strip normal data and $\\rho_k$ is the decreasing perturbation or background error. The derivative of $h$ is bounded by the same normal size and error. Its total drift is therefore bounded independently of $T$, and on middle strips the field is exponentially close to a single, possibly varying, middle flat.*\n\n*These assertions include a central $\\alpha$, in whose fixed slice $h$ has three real coordinates. They give matching up to $H$, exponential convergence on completed ends, and convergence of holonomies uniformly over compact smooth families of bounded paths on the relevant strips. At isolated lens flats the same assertions hold with no harmonic spatial term.",
        "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-ordinary-neck-decay",
          "exact_quote": "Give $L=S^1\\times S^2$ the product metric, and let $\\alpha$ be a flat connection with parallel stabilizer $H$. On a sufficiently small-energy neck, modulo gauge, the spatial field has the form $$\\label{eq:ordinary:harmonic-slice}\n a(t)=\\alpha+h(t)\\vartheta+b(t),\n \\quad h(t)\\in H^0_\\alpha(L;\\operatorname{ad}),\n \\quad b(t)\\perp H^1_\\alpha(L;\\operatorname{ad}),\n \\quad d_\\alpha^*b(t)=0.$$ Here $\\vartheta$ is the circle one-form and the temporal component has zero parallel part. For $[-T,T]$ and any sufficiently small fixed decay rate $\\delta>0$, the normal part satisfies estimates of the form $$\\label{eq:ordinary:normal-decay}\n \\|b(t)\\|_{k}\n \\le C_k\\bigl(B_-e^{-\\delta(t+T)}\n                  +B_+e^{-\\delta(T-t)}\\bigr)\n       +C_k\\int_{-T}^T e^{-\\delta|t-s|}\\rho_k(s)\\,ds,$$ where $B_\\pm$ measure the end-strip normal data and $\\rho_k$ is the decreasing perturbation or background error. The derivative of $h$ is bounded by the same normal size and error. Its total drift is therefore bounded independently of $T$, and on middle strips the field is exponentially close to a single, possibly varying, middle flat.*\n\n*These assertions include a central $\\alpha$, in whose fixed slice $h$ has three real coordinates. They give matching up to $H$, exponential convergence on completed ends, and convergence of holonomies uniformly over compact smooth families of bounded paths on the relevant strips. At isolated lens flats the same assertions hold with no harmonic spatial term.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-ordinary-regular-gluing",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose two completed ordinary pieces meet at one of the auxiliary flats above. Assume that one piece is a cap whose parallel stabilizer is the whole matching group $H$; it has one matching end, and its other end conditions, if present, are decaying. Assume that the connection on the other piece is irreducible; prescribed unglued true-end asymptotes are also irreducible. Frame the cap at the matching end and leave the other piece unframed. Suppose the matched half-problem, including all flat parameters, metric parameters and cuts, is isolated and transverse. Then for all sufficiently long necks each such match gives exactly one solution modulo determinant-one gauge. Every convergent solution sufficiently close to this broken configuration arises in this way. The regular operators and gauge-fixing operators have inverses with at most polynomial growth in neck length.*\n\n*The assertion also holds for successive removal of pendant caps in a tree of regular cuts, provided each removal satisfies these hypotheses with compatible data.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-ordinary-central-cost",
        "exact_quote": "In a broken ordinary configuration, let a maximal consecutive group consist of $q$ reducible pieces or levels with only central rational contacts.         "exact_quote": "With the signs of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:negative:local-sign\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:negative:local-sign\">25</a>, $B$ is an integral chain map.         "anchor": "stmt-thm-caps-pairing",
        "exact_quote": "There are two fixed compact caps $C_-$ and $C_+$ with common rational boundary $Y_2$, fixed determinant data trivialized at that boundary, and finite collections of integral point and surface probes in their interiors with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *Each cap has $H_1(C_\\pm;\\mathbb Z)=0$ and $b^+(C_\\pm)>0$. Each contains a square-zero copy of $A$ on which the determinant class evaluates as $1$, and a tight genus-two surface of square two.*\n\n2.  *Each cap has one additional, separate exceptional summand. The determinant evaluates as zero on its exceptional sphere, and every probe is supported in the old part of the cap.*\n\n3.  *For suitable generic cap data and small ordinary Floer data at the rational boundary, the cut counts give a rational cycle $x$ and a rational cocycle $y$ on the irreducible determinant-one Floer complex, with $$\\label{eq:caps:nonzero-pairing}\n                             yx\\ne0.$$ Fixed integral multiples of these are an integral cycle and cocycle.*\n\n4.  *The total real degree $z$ of all cap probes is fixed. Reducible cap limits in any of the bounded charge ranges used below are excluded by the cap period choices. The period choices admit the finite isolation extensions of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:estimates:cap\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:estimates:cap\">72</a>.*\n\n*The cycle and cocycle can be recomputed with the final cap data used in Section <a href=\"#sec:stack\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:stack\">5</a>; their pairing is the same nonzero closed Donaldson count, up to the fixed normalization and orientation sign.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-stack-tests",
        "exact_quote": "The sphere tests can be chosen with the following properties, preserving the integral map $B$ on homology and its mod-two unit property. For a commuting connection whose ordered line difference is $v$, a whole test avoids $-1$ if $vS_i=0$. Toward the primary face it becomes two consecutive sweeps representing $F_{l,i}$ and $-F_{r,i}$; each sweep then avoids $-1$ when its half evaluation is zero. During the change of prescription, avoidance is retained if both half evaluations vanish. At an actual $J_i$-split each surviving test is assigned compactly to exactly one side. At a lens face it is supported on the lens cap and its data at the two determinant lifts are tensor-paired as in Proposition <a href=\"#prop:negative:local-sign\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:negative:local-sign\">25</a>.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-stack-charge-costs",
        "exact_quote": "For the main pieces of a single interval or macro, virtually restore all separated lens caps with the split references of differences $0,\\pm4,\\pm2$, respectively at the extendibly central, other central, and trace-zero states.         "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },
      "evidence": [

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-stack-composition",
        "exact_quote": "Choose the old cap metrics with generic periods and take sufficiently long finite isolation collars for their separate extra exceptional summands.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-stack-finite-lattice",
        "exact_quote": "Let $C,C'$ be finite complexes of finitely generated free abelian groups, and let $f:C\\to C'$ be a chain map whose reduction modulo two is a quasi-isomorphism. On the free quotients $$L=H(C;\\mathbb Z)/\\operatorname{Tor},\\qquad\n L'=H(C';\\mathbb Z)/\\operatorname{Tor},$$ its induced map is an isomorphism after localization at two. In particular $L/2^NL\\to L'/2^NL'$ is an isomorphism for every $N\\ge1$.*\n\n*If $L=L'$ has rank $r$, all these maps modulo $2^N$ have orders dividing a single integer depending only on $r,N$.",
        "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-thm-stack-nonzero",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the old caps and their compact probes. Prescribe any lower bounds on the two outside pad lengths, and prescribe any odd evaluations of $\\Lambda$ on their separate extra exceptional classes. There exist arbitrarily large finite stacks with positive bridges at spacing four, satisfying those pad bounds, for which the following hold simultaneously:*\n\n1.  *the lifts are those of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:stack:lifts\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:stack:lifts\">44</a>, with a common allowed charge $\\kappa$ and $D_I=n+z$;*\n\n2.  *the actual oriented ordinary family count satisfies $\\Omega\\ne0$;*\n\n3.  *the coupled Dirac index $n_D=\\Theta-\\kappa$ is positive;*\n\n4.  *all auxiliary collars are finite, and the metric and small-data choices can be made to satisfy Theorem <a href=\"#thm:geometry:family\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:geometry:family\">54</a> and Theorem <a href=\"#thm:estimates:clamp\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:estimates:clamp\">64</a>.*\n\n*The integers specifying the stack and all topological lift data are chosen before the artificial isolation sizes, perturbation bounds, and external Floer gluing lengths.",

      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-geometry-family",
        "exact_quote": "For the fixed finite stack, there are families with the following properties. They are defined for all sufficiently small $\\epsilon>0$, all sufficiently small regularizers $d>0$, and arbitrarily long finite auxiliary rational collars. The auxiliary bounds may depend on $\\epsilon$ and the fixed problem. The family parameter is the original cube of interval parameters, with no added boundary faces.*\n\n1.  *At its genuine faces the family has independent product length collars at $J_i$ and $\\partial N_i$, compatible at intersections of faces. The $J_i$ cross-sections are round. On a component separated by $J_i$, the limiting data depend only on the interval parameters retained on that component. The $N_i$ metric is complete with positive scalar curvature and a positive-scalar-curvature product end. Its link and its scale on the stretching collar are independent of the tangential cube parameters. The link is joined to the round lens metric through positive-scalar-curvature metrics. These metric choices are common to the two bit terms compared at that lens face.*\n\n\n2.  *On the positive-width toric region of a macro constructed below, as $d\\to0$ the retained main piece has a complete metric conformal to a toric Kähler metric with positive cohomology ray represented by $$H=U+aX_1+b_0X_2,\\qquad\n     0\\le a,b_0\\le\\tfrac14,\\qquad a+b_0>0.\n     \\label{eq:geometry:period}$$ It has nonnegative scalar curvature, with strict positivity on an open set. A zero coefficient removes the corresponding outer part by a $C_{1,i}$ separation; a coefficient $1/4$ separates $N_i$. The class $H$ is supported rationally on the retained main piece in all these cases. Its positive rank is one.*\n\n\n3.  *Every macro in the small-width replacement region contains an $S^2\\times S^1\\times I$ tube, with fiber $U$, of length comparable to $\\epsilon^{-1}$. On its bulk the metric is, or approaches smoothly, $$g_{\\mathrm{long}}\n     =g_{S^2(1/\\sqrt2)}+\\tfrac12\\,d\\xi^2+2\\,d\\theta_x^2.\n     \\label{eq:geometry:long-model}$$ The same description holds for every toric macro whose normalized length $L=1/(a+b_0)$ tends to infinity. All such tube lengths are $O(\\epsilon^{-1})$. The tubes lie in $C_0$ and are disjoint from both middle spheres $J_i$.*\n\n4.  *Along any sequence of these parameters, every additional unbounded region is one of the following: an exact rational product collar, an annulus approaching a positive-scalar-curvature product, or one of the tubes in <span class=\"upright\">(iii)</span>. The remaining pieces, after the specified satellite rescalings, have uniformly bounded geometry on fixed truncations. There are only finitely many such pieces for the fixed stack. Away from fixed-length tube ends, the error from <a href=\"#eq:geometry:long-model\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:geometry:long-model\">[eq:geometry:long-model]</a>, with any fixed number of spatial derivatives, tends to zero as the distance from both ends tends to infinity. In particular the integrated errors used in Section <a href=\"#sec:estimates\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:estimates\">7</a> are $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$, uniformly under deeper regularization and longer auxiliary rational collars. For scalar-curvature costs, the middles of the $Y_j$ collars are omitted, retaining prefixes of length $O(\\epsilon^{-1/2})$; no positivity is required on a $Y_j$ cross-section.*\n\n5.  *For each fixed real cohomology class $\\Lambda$ there are closed comparison forms with its prescribed vertical flux on these tubes, zero curvature on the long parts of rational collars, and $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$ energy away from the tubes. More precisely, the uniform comparison and error assertions are those of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:geometry:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:geometry:comparison\">63</a>.*\n\n*The construction is smooth at finite parameter values and has the ordinary product description on every genuine length collar. Only spatial derivative estimates are asserted uniformly as lengths diverge; no bound on derivatives in a compactifying length coordinate is needed.",
        "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },
      "evidence": [

A zero coefficient removes the corresponding outer part by a $C_{1,i}$ separation; a coefficient $1/4$ separates $N_i$. The class $H$ is supported rationally on the retained main piece in all these cases. Its positive rank is one.*\n\n\n3.  *Every macro in the small-width replacement region contains an $S^2\\times S^1\\times I$ tube, with fiber $U$, of length comparable to $\\epsilon^{-1}$. On its bulk the metric is, or approaches smoothly, $$g_{\\mathrm{long}}\n     =g_{S^2(1/\\sqrt2)}+\\tfrac12\\,d\\xi^2+2\\,d\\theta_x^2.\n     \\label{eq:geometry:long-model}$$ The same description holds for every toric macro whose normalized length $L=1/(a+b_0)$ tends to infinity. All such tube lengths are $O(\\epsilon^{-1})$. The tubes lie in $C_0$ and are disjoint from both middle spheres $J_i$.*\n\n4.  *Along any sequence of these parameters, every additional unbounded region is one of the following: an exact rational product collar, an annulus approaching a positive-scalar-curvature product, or one of the tubes in <span class=\"upright\">(iii)</span>. The remaining pieces, after the specified satellite rescalings, have uniformly bounded geometry on fixed truncations. There are only finitely many such pieces for the fixed stack. Away from fixed-length tube ends, the error from <a href=\"#eq:geometry:long-model\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:geometry:long-model\">[eq:geometry:long-model]</a>, with any fixed number of spatial derivatives, tends to zero as the distance from both ends tends to infinity. In particular the integrated errors used in Section <a href=\"#sec:estimates\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:estimates\">7</a> are $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$, uniformly under deeper regularization and longer auxiliary rational collars. For scalar-curvature costs, the middles of the $Y_j$ collars are omitted, retaining prefixes of length $O(\\epsilon^{-1/2})$; no positivity is required on a $Y_j$ cross-section.*\n\n5.  *For each fixed real cohomology class $\\Lambda$ there are closed comparison forms with its prescribed vertical flux on these tubes, zero curvature on the long parts of rational collars, and $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$ energy away from the tubes. More precisely, the uniform comparison and error assertions are those of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:geometry:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:geometry:comparison\">63</a>.*\n\n*The construction is smooth at finite parameter values and has the ordinary product description on every genuine length collar. Only spatial derivative estimates are asserted uniformly as lengths diverge; no bound on derivatives in a compactifying length coordinate is needed.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $l_\\nu$ be positive affine functions with gradients $n_\\nu$ spanning $\\mathbb R^2$, and let $C\\ge0$ be constant. For every nonzero relation $\\sum_\\nu\\gamma_\\nu n_\\nu=0$, its two nonnegative terms satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n q^t(I-P)q\n &\\ge \\frac{(\\sum_\\nu\\gamma_\\nu P_{\\nu\\nu})^2}\n                    {\\sum_\\nu\\gamma_\\nu^2l_\\nu},\n \\label{eq:geometry:first-bound}\\\\\n z^t\\bigl((I-P)\\circ(P\\circ P)\\bigr)z\n &\\ge\\frac{\\left\\|\\sum_\\nu\\gamma_\\nu A_\\nu A_\\nu^t\\right\\|_{\\mathrm{HS}}^2}\n                   {\\sum_\\nu\\gamma_\\nu^2l_\\nu}.\n \\label{eq:geometry:second-bound}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The main metrics have strictly positive scalar curvature on compact sets away from punctures, including their smooth toric axes.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-geometry-collars",
        "exact_quote": "For every fixed derivative order $k$, the metric near an edge with shrink parameter $\\delta=r_i$ or $h_i$ has the following description. There is a homogeneous radius $R$ and a cone metric $g_{\\mathrm c}$ such that, in scale-invariant $C^k$ norms on every dyadic annulus, $$\\|g-g_{\\mathrm c}\\|_{C^k(g_{\\mathrm c})}\n \\le C_k\\bigl(\\delta/R^2+R^2\\bigr),\n \\qquad C\\sqrt\\delta\\le R\\le R_*.\n \\label{eq:geometry:cone-error}$$ The estimates include smooth toric axes and are uniform on the $L\\to\\infty$ tips. In affine moment coordinates $\\mu_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ centered at the relevant homogeneous cone vertex, the scale $\\mu_{\\mathrm{loc}}=\\delta\\widehat\\mu_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ gives $g=\\delta(g_{\\mathrm{sat}}+o(1))$ on compact sets away from any remaining cone point. The metric $g_{\\mathrm{sat}}$ is a three-direction Hessian metric with strictly positive scalar curvature on those compact sets.*\n\n*There are conformal changes making all the necessary annuli asymptotically cylindrical, with fixed positive limiting link sizes. They have nonnegative scalar curvature and preserve strict positivity on smooth compact regions. Arbitrarily deep in those annuli one may interpolate to the exact limiting product over a bounded logarithmic width, with $C^k$ errors tending to zero. In particular the separated $N_i$ cap can be made positive everywhere, including its exact product end.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-geometry-period-support",
        "exact_quote": "Let $H$ be a positive-width limiting period in <a href=\"#eq:geometry:period\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:geometry:period\">[eq:geometry:period]</a>. Express it as a convex combination of the four vertex classes $$U,\\qquad U+X_1/4,\\qquad U+X_2/4,\n \\qquad U+(X_1+X_2)/4.$$ Every vertex with nonzero weight is carried rationally by the retained smooth main piece. It omits every side whose coefficient is zero, and is orthogonal to every divisor whose coefficient is $1/4$. Its pairings may consequently be computed with compactly supported Poincaré forms on that piece, independently of any reference filling at a true lens cut. A side occurring in such a nonempty vertex still has its whole-sphere test in the approximating positive-width family.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-geometry-comparison",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a finite set of real degree-two classes on the fixed stack, or on its genuine-cut components with specified bounded reference extensions. On every family in Theorem <a href=\"#thm:geometry:family\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:geometry:family\">54</a> each such class $\\Lambda$ has a closed imaginary-valued representative $b_*$, with $b_*/(2\\pi i)$ representing $\\Lambda$, such that the following hold. On each long tube of fiber $U$ it is $$b_*=i\\lambda_U\\,\\operatorname{vol}_{S^2(1/\\sqrt2)},\n \\qquad \\lambda_U=\\Lambda U,\n \\label{eq:geometry:comparison-flux}$$ apart from bounded end transitions. It vanishes on the long middle of every rational collar. For every fixed truncation size $T$, its energy off the bulk tubes is bounded by a constant $C_T$ on all compact and rescaled pieces, independently of deeper regularizations and longer rational collars. On the tube bulk its norm and volume differ from their product values by an error of the form <a href=\"#eq:geometry:integrated-error\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:geometry:integrated-error\">[eq:geometry:integrated-error]</a>. Consequently $$\\int |b_*|^2=O(\\epsilon^{-1}),\\qquad\n \\int_{\\mathrm{off\\ tubes}}|b_*|^2=o(\\epsilon^{-1}),\n \\label{eq:geometry:comparison-energy}$$ where bounded end regions may be included in either term. The same uniform $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$ assertion holds for the squared negative scalar-curvature costs on the region obtained by omitting the $Y_j$ middles and retaining prefixes of length $O(\\epsilon^{-1/2})$, and for bounded local defects from the bulk model. There is no scalar-curvature assertion on the omitted $Y_j$ middles. Constants may depend on the fixed classes and finite problem. These assertions do not assert uniform bounds as the integral class itself ranges over an unbounded set.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-estimates-clamp",
        "exact_quote": "For the finite problem $\\mathcal P$ and a fixed upper bound on total topological charge, the metrics and fixed line connections of Theorem <a href=\"#thm:geometry:family\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:geometry:family\">54</a> can be chosen with all artificial isolation lengths finite so that the following assertions hold simultaneously, including at every genuine face.*\n\n\n1.  *On an $R$ or $S$ component containing a positive bridge, either $u=0$, or there is a nonempty subset $I$ of its adjacent whole sides such that $$\\operatorname{sign}(u)z_I\\leq0\\quad(R),\n       \\qquad\n       \\operatorname{sign}(u)z_I<|\\lambda_I|\\quad(S).\n       \\label{eq:estimates:clamp}$$*\n\n2.  *No $R$ component contains an outside cap. For each fixed old cap $W$, cut at its rational seams and before its extra blow-up, there is a constant $C_W$ such that an $S$ component satisfies $$v_W^2\\leq C_W,\\qquad (\\Lambda_W+v_W)^2\\leq C_W.\n           \\label{eq:estimates:cap-squares}$$ The constant depends only on $W$, its fixed line data, metric and boundary collars. It is independent of the number of added intervals and of the new exceptional evaluations.*\n\n3.  *On an actually separated $N_i$ the fixed background is harmonic and anti-self-dual, and the metric has positive scalar curvature. The complementary metrics and backgrounds agree for the two bit choices differing by the class supported on $N_i$.*\n\n*One may first choose a positive bound for the ordinary Floer-gradient perturbations on the finite $Y$ seams and then take those seams to any sufficiently large finite gluing lengths. Once those lengths have been chosen, further compatible perturbations may be made sufficiently small, including in total squared $L^2$ cost on the seams. Precise quantifiers are given in Corollary <a href=\"#cor:estimates:choices\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"cor:estimates:choices\">73</a>.*\n\n*The charge assumption concerns the sum over all retained fields and nonnegative ideal losses. No sign assumption is made on the charge of an arbitrary $\\operatorname{PU}(2)$ component.",
        "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-estimates-hodge",
        "exact_quote": "On a completed piece with rational-homology-sphere ends, a real cohomology class has a unique $L^2$ harmonic representative. If pieces are joined by increasingly long product collars with rational cross-sections, their harmonic representatives converge on compact subsets to the representatives of the restricted classes, provided their total norms are bounded. The convergence and the cutoff errors are exponential in distance from the ends of a long collar.*\n\n*Background connections can consequently be chosen to be flat on the middle of each sufficiently long finite $Y$ collar and to obey the product rule at all genuine faces. On an isolated positive toric piece their self-dual curvature is proportional to its Kähler form; on a separated $N_i$ it is zero.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-estimates-cylinder",
        "exact_quote": "Consider a flat-background product cylinder with fixed cross-section $Y$. On its translation-invariant middle, assume that the ordinary connection perturbation is the gradient of a functional $\\mathcal W$ with $\\|\\mathcal W\\|_\\infty\\leq M$ and uniformly bounded gradient. Let $r,e$ denote any additional connection and Dirac errors there. Suppose their total squared $L^2$ norms are bounded by $\\nu$. There is a constant $C_Y$, depending only on the fixed cross-section and the functional and gradient bounds, independent of both $\\nu$ and cylinder length, such that one can choose boundary slices in prescribed interior unit strips near its two ends for which $$\\kappa_{\\rm middle}\\geq-C_Y-C_Y\\nu.\n                  \\label{eq:estimates:cylinder-charge}$$ The complementary bounded strips may be included in the retained region of a cutoff estimate.",
        "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },

For harmonic backgrounds, and also for the product-rule backgrounds of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:estimates:hodge\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:estimates:hodge\">65</a> chosen with smaller errors, $$\\sum_{\\mathcal T}\\|\\beta-\\lambda_{\\mathcal T}\\omega_{S^2}\\|_{L^2(\\mathcal T)}^2\n   +\\|\\beta\\|_{L^2(\\mathrm{rest})}^2=o_{\\mathcal P}(\\epsilon^{-1}),\n \\qquad \\|\\beta\\|_2^2=O_{\\mathcal P}(\\epsilon^{-1}).\n \\label{eq:estimates:tube-background}$$ Here $\\mathcal T$ runs over the bulk tubes, bounded end pieces may be transferred to the rest, and $\\omega_{S^2}$ is the area form of $S^2(1/\\sqrt2)$. The subscript on the little-$o$ means uniformity over those admissible choices and all parameter faces for the fixed problem.*\n\n\n*For solutions whose total charge is bounded above, bounded ordinary $Y$ gradient perturbations and additional errors of squared cost $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$ give $$\\int_{\\mathcal R_\\epsilon}\n       (|\\Phi|^4+|F_a^{0,+}|^2+|F_a^0|^2)\n                  =o_{\\mathcal P}(\\epsilon^{-1}).\n \\label{eq:estimates:small-energy}$$ For each fixed $\\epsilon>0$, the same quantities have a finite bound $E_{\\mathcal P,\\epsilon}$ independent of all subsequently lengthened rational collars and of the omitted $Y$ lengths, with the error costs bounded.         "exact_quote": "The constants $C_W$ can be fixed before choosing the delays, exceptional evaluations and repetition count in the stack.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-analysis-regularization",
        "exact_quote": "For the fixed finite family, equation perturbations and representatives can be chosen arbitrarily small in the prescribed norms with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *Ordinary irreducible equations and the labelled sphere, surface, and point tests are transverse, including the relevant ideal and broken strata. Their representatives have the exact support and persistence properties of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:analysis:incidence\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:analysis:incidence\">99</a>. They are compatible with fixed determinant gluing, marked translation on cylinders, and all true faces. Prescribed harmonic reducers on separated caps are preserved.*\n\n2.  *Single-component, single-valued equivariant perturbations give the fixed-type regularity in Definition <a href=\"#def:indices:analytic-hypotheses\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:indices:analytic-hypotheses\">80</a>. Every tuple of fixed type is consequently excluded except the legitimate unbroken cut-down instantons.*\n\n3.  *A finite collection of rational multisection terms, in addition to single-valued terms, eliminates every forbidden mixed ideal stratum by the negative dimension of its necessary projection. No equation or retained cut on this projection depends on discarded $R$ fields or their particles. The allowed free stratum is regular of dimension one, and the single trace-end main problem is regular of dimension zero. Choices on the exterior of a separated lens cap agree under the corresponding bit flip.*\n\n4.  *Solutions have the compactness, removable-singularity, integral particle-charge, and exponential true-end properties proved below. Near each legitimate instanton, the phase-cut link has oriented count $2^\\eta$ times its instanton sign, where $\\eta=n_D^{\\rm tot}-1$.*\n\n*The finite branch lists have compatible weighted germs and total weight one. After the no-particle end gluing of Section <a href=\"#sec:gluing\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:gluing\">10</a>, their oriented one-dimensional zero sets obey the ordinary rational Stokes rule.",
        "source_id": "PM-306.1"
      },

        "exact_quote": "Put $n_*=n_D^{\\rm tot}>0$ and $\\eta=n_*-1$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Surgery slopes and purely cosmetic fillings** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Two distinct slopes giving orientation-preservingly homeomorphic fillings are called *purely cosmetic*.
- **Ordinary homology unit** ([source](#sec:ordinary)): The word “unit” means an isomorphism on instanton homology over $\mathbb F_2$; it does not assert that a particular matrix on the chain group is invertible.
- **Fixed-limit unframed index** ([source](#stmt-conv-ordinary-index)): On a completed piece, $i$ denotes the unframed ASD index with the boundary representatives fixed.
- **Tight surface** ([source](#sec:caps)): A *tight surface* is an embedded oriented surface $B$ with $B^2=2g(B)-2>0$.
- **Finite label ring** ([source](#pm-h-23)): Keep the labels distinct and set $$\label{eq:caps:label-ring} L_a=\mathbb Q[t_1,\ldots,t_a]/(t_1^2,\ldots,t_a^2), \qquad J=(t_1,\ldots,t_a).$$
- **Macro** ([source](#pm-h-26)): A positive bridge together with its two adjacent negative intervals is a *macro*.
- **Characteristic spin data** ([source](#pm-h-27)): For a rank-two bundle with determinant class $c$, write $\Lambda=l+c$.
- **Genuine length** ([source](#sec:geometry)): A *genuine length* is a length tending to infinity at a face of the interval cube.
- **Fixed finite problem** ([source](#sec:estimates)): This means that the number of intervals, the bits, the bundles, all exceptional evaluations, the charge bound, and the finite set of reference fillings have been fixed.
- **Field types and fixed-type tuples** ([source](#stmt-def-indices-types)): The phase circle $\mathbb T$ acts by multiplying $\Phi$. On the quotient by determinant-one gauge, its kernel at a free orbit is $\{1,-1\}$. A main component has type $A$ when $\Phi=0$ and the connection is irreducible, type $R$ when $\Phi=0$ and the connection has continuous stabilizer, type $S$ when $\Phi\ne0$ lies in one summand of a parallel splitting, and type $P$ otherwise. A *fixed-type tuple* has no component of type $P$. The letters here denote field types; in particular $A$ is not the capped Seifert surface, and $P$ is not the positive bridge cell. For a split connection write $E=L_1\oplus L_2$ and $v=c_1(L_1)-c_1(L_2)$, placing the active spinor line first in type $S$. Then $$\label{eq:indices:split-classes} v\equiv c\pmod2,\qquad K=l+2c_1(L_1)=\Lambda+v.$$ At type $R$ choose either ordering, including an ordering at a central connection. Actual separated lens caps are not counted as main components when assigning these types.
- **Split line difference** ([source](#stmt-def-indices-types)): For a split connection write $E=L_1\oplus L_2$ and $v=c_1(L_1)-c_1(L_2)$, placing the active spinor line first in type $S$.
- **Admissibility for exclusion** ([source](#stmt-def-indices-analytic-hypotheses)): Call a choice of equations and representatives *admissible for the exclusion calculation* if it has the following properties, for all ideal main-part tuples in the fixed total charge budget, including the enlarged candidate class described in Section <a href="#subsec:analysis:candidates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="subsec:analysis:candidates">9.6</a>. In this class the completed main fields satisfy their equations and retained nonphase cuts, together with the phase cuts when imposed. Matching across true cuts and the actual lens-cap and connector fields are omitted. The assigned lens-cap and connector charges obey their permitted nonnegative ranges and the total charge constraint; the omitted fields need not be realizable. 1. On a fixed-type tuple, the restricted ASD equations with retained nonphase cuts on type $A$ components, and the pure tangential equations on type $S$ components, are transverse. In particular a type $A$ component has $q_i\ge0$, with strict inequality if it has any lens end, main particle, or allocated nonconstant $J$-trajectory loss. A type $S$ component satisfies $$\label{eq:indices:tangential-bound} d_s+p_i+4\ell_i\ge0.$$ These are componentwise assertions using only parameters retained on the component. 2. For types $R,S$, an assigned whole sphere test with $v(S_j)=0$ requires a unit of $\ell_i$. This includes a separated lens test. During switching to the $J$ prescription the unit is required if both half values vanish; at a true $J$ the assigned test requires the unit if its own half value vanishes. Different sphere tests so charged on the same component require distinct units. Type $S$ is needed in this assertion only for a tuple with no $P$. 3. For a tuple containing $P$, project away all type $R$ fields, positions, and tests, retaining their parameters. The equations and retained cuts on the other components are independent of the discarded data. Before diagonal phase quotient and phase cuts, the necessary projected problem has dimension at most $$\label{eq:indices:projection-input} \sum_{i\notin R} \left(i_i-\sum_{\text{lens ends of }i}(\delta_{\rm sp}-1)-2w_i\right) +\sum_{i\in R}p_i,$$ where $w_i$ is the total main-particle weight and other allocated integer loss outside lens caps on that component. The $\eta$ phase sections subtract $2\eta$, and the phase quotient subtracts one. Regularity is required only near the projections of candidate tuples in the stated overcount, with all $R$ fields still present before projection. At those candidate projections, a negative dimension excludes a zero. No assertion is made about other zeros of the enlarged equations after the $R$ fields are discarded. This permits finite rational multisections on free strata without changing the integral instanton maps at zero spinor.
- **Candidate** ([source](#subsec:analysis:candidates)): A *candidate* consists of completed main fields, their parameter values, weighted main particles, retained cut variables, and a discrete charge assignment.
- **Framed minimal cap** ([source](#pm-h-62)): On $N$, *framed* means quotienting by gauge transformations tending to the identity at this fixed representative.

| q-outside-active-line-score | Shifted instanton score of an outside active-line component | ≥ | $8$ | Includes a component containing both caps; choices precede middle repetition and finite metric isolation. |
| q-instanton-link-multiplicity | Oriented link count | = | $2^\eta\,\operatorname{sign}(a)$ | Regular isolated ordinary instanton with surjective coupled Dirac operator. |

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-geometry-comparison",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a finite set of real degree-two classes on the fixed stack, or on its genuine-cut components with specified bounded reference extensions. On every family in Theorem <a href=\"#thm:geometry:family\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:geometry:family\">54</a> each such class $\\Lambda$ has a closed imaginary-valued representative $b_*$, with $b_*/(2\\pi i)$ representing $\\Lambda$, such that the following hold. On each long tube of fiber $U$ it is $$b_*=i\\lambda_U\\,\\operatorname{vol}_{S^2(1/\\sqrt2)},\n \\qquad \\lambda_U=\\Lambda U,\n \\label{eq:geometry:comparison-flux}$$ apart from bounded end transitions. It vanishes on the long middle of every rational collar. For every fixed truncation size $T$, its energy off the bulk tubes is bounded by a constant $C_T$ on all compact and rescaled pieces, independently of deeper regularizations and longer rational collars. On the tube bulk its norm and volume differ from their product values by an error of the form <a href=\"#eq:geometry:integrated-error\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:geometry:integrated-error\">[eq:geometry:integrated-error]</a>. Consequently $$\\int |b_*|^2=O(\\epsilon^{-1}),\\qquad\n \\int_{\\mathrm{off\\ tubes}}|b_*|^2=o(\\epsilon^{-1}),\n \\label{eq:geometry:comparison-energy}$$ where bounded end regions may be included in either term. The same uniform $o(\\epsilon^{-1})$ assertion holds for the squared negative scalar-curvature costs on the region obtained by omitting the $Y_j$ middles and retaining prefixes of length $O(\\epsilon^{-1/2})$, and for bounded local defects from the bulk model. There is no scalar-curvature assertion on the omitted $Y_j$ middles. Constants may depend on the fixed classes and finite problem. These assertions do not assert uniform bounds as the integral class itself ranges over an unbounded set.",

          "anchor": "stmt-thm-estimates-clamp",
          "exact_quote": "For the finite problem $\\mathcal P$ and a fixed upper bound on total topological charge, the metrics and fixed line connections of Theorem <a href=\"#thm:geometry:family\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:geometry:family\">54</a> can be chosen with all artificial isolation lengths finite so that the following assertions hold simultaneously, including at every genuine face.*\n\n\n1.  *On an $R$ or $S$ component containing a positive bridge, either $u=0$, or there is a nonempty subset $I$ of its adjacent whole sides such that $$\\operatorname{sign}(u)z_I\\leq0\\quad(R),\n       \\qquad\n       \\operatorname{sign}(u)z_I<|\\lambda_I|\\quad(S).\n       \\label{eq:estimates:clamp}$$*\n\n2.  *No $R$ component contains an outside cap. For each fixed old cap $W$, cut at its rational seams and before its extra blow-up, there is a constant $C_W$ such that an $S$ component satisfies $$v_W^2\\leq C_W,\\qquad (\\Lambda_W+v_W)^2\\leq C_W.\n           \\label{eq:estimates:cap-squares}$$ The constant depends only on $W$, its fixed line data, metric and boundary collars. It is independent of the number of added intervals and of the new exceptional evaluations.*\n\n3.  *On an actually separated $N_i$ the fixed background is harmonic and anti-self-dual, and the metric has positive scalar curvature. Once those lengths have been chosen, further compatible perturbations may be made sufficiently small, including in total squared $L^2$ cost on the seams. <a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-slope-reduction** [claim](#stmt-prop-introduction-reduction) / [proof](#pm-h-3): Combine the cited slope restrictions, first homology, and the meridional filling obstruction. -> A hypothetical distinct oriented cosmetic pair supplies the fixed remaining surgery identification.
- **step-ordinary-end-and-index-framework** [claim](#stmt-lem-ordinary-index) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ordinary-index): Classify rational reducible flats and retain the unframed stabilizer correction in charge and excision formulas. -> Fixed-limit index bookkeeping and length-independent gradient energy control.
- **step-handle-family-construction** [claim](#stmt-lem-ordinary-metric-families) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ordinary-metric-families): Use smooth polygon quotients and noncrossing collar systems, then compute their determinant and intersection data. -> Compatible interval, pentagon, and compressed families with their complete face lists.
- **step-ordinary-regularity-and-matching** [claim](#stmt-lem-ordinary-regular-gluing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ordinary-regular-gluing): Construct componentwise holonomy variations and gradient trajectory variations; separate harmonic neck modes and absorb matching rotations on single-ended caps. -> Regular and exhaustive ordinary matching charts with coherent orientations.
- **step-unit-compactification-budget** [claim](#stmt-lem-ordinary-low-dimensional-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ordinary-low-dimensional-compactness): Compare elementary cap shifts and central-group costs against the dimensions available on each primary face. -> Only the listed ordinary chain breaks, compositions, and paired minimum cap matches remain.
- **step-hard-cap-degree** [claim](#stmt-lem-ordinary-holonomy-degree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ordinary-holonomy-degree): Replace the hard cap by the flat product filling, compute minimum harmonic paths, and track normalized eigenholonomy including determinant signs. -> The outer face contributes the continuation operation with odd parity.
- **step-ordinary-units-and-bridge** [claim](#stmt-thm-ordinary-units) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ordinary-cap-end-compactness-2): Read the compactified pentagon boundary identities and compose the rigid units through the fixed surgery identification. -> Ordinary homology units and an integral bridge that is a rational quasi-isomorphism.
- **step-negative-cap-and-signs** [claim](#stmt-prop-negative-local-sign) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-negative-local-sign): Compute the minimum order-four cap and compare its tensor-related full deformation-and-cut orientation lines. -> An integral negative chain map with coherent local cancellation and compatible homotopy invariance.
- **step-negative-modular-unit** [claim](#stmt-thm-negative-unit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-negative-sweeps-2): Compute the four-step facet relation, identify the selected central flat by root mismatch, and contract the surviving pentagon loop through complementary disks. -> The signed integral negative map induces a homology isomorphism modulo two.
- **step-closure-model-nonvanishing** [claim](#stmt-prop-caps-nonvanishing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-caps-model-2): Build an enhanced symplectic closure; isolate extremal generalized Floer lines; extract the pencil word from products of elliptic model words; apply simple type and blowup comparison. -> A nonzero closed Donaldson invariant for the prescribed determinant.
- **step-labelled-positive-power** [claim](#stmt-lem-caps-positive-power) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-caps-positive-power): Use exact-support particle budgets and fixed-transition closed comparison to construct the finite labelled deformation, then apply the characteristic-polynomial identity on homology. -> A positive bridge power has a nonzero all-label cap pairing.
- **step-fixed-cap-states** [claim](#stmt-thm-caps-pairing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-caps-periods-2): Split homology at a rational seam, allocate all probes to cap interiors, isolate the separate exceptional summands, and exclude cap reducers by periods. -> Fixed integral multiples of cap cycles and cocycles with a nonzero rational pairing.
- **step-stack-lattice-and-lifts** [claim](#stmt-lem-stack-telescope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-stack-telescope): Compute unimodular cell bases and characteristic lift restrictions, then telescope endpoint-bit contributions across the stack. -> Global and component index formulas with controlled positive-cell spacing.
- **step-macro-and-closed-composition** [claim](#stmt-prop-stack-composition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-stack-composition): Install compatible sphere tests, charge every reducer assignment, establish the relative macro map, and use local excess plus seam stabilizers to exclude central external matches. -> The final ordinary count equals the composition of cap states and ordinary factor maps.
- **step-finite-lattice-repetition** [claim](#stmt-thm-stack-nonzero) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-stack-nonzero): Pass to the free integral homology quotient, use finite orders modulo a power of two, and choose repetitions satisfying the bundle-degree congruence. -> A finite stack has a nonzero integral ordinary count and positive coupled Dirac index.
- **step-toric-positive-scalar-sectors** [claim](#stmt-lem-geometry-collars) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-geometry-collars): Place the embedded interfaces, construct the punctured polygon Hessian, prove its nonnegative scalar identity, and conformally complete cone and satellite regions. -> Positive-width metric sectors and compatible positive lens-cap ends.
- **step-global-metric-assembly** [claim](#stmt-thm-geometry-family) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-geometry-comparison): Assemble saturation collars on a fixed macro, replace the low-width corner by a spherical tube, retain supported period vertices, and build uniform comparison forms. -> A simultaneous family with exactly the prescribed genuine cuts and controlled auxiliary regions.
- **step-retained-energy-and-zero-flux** [claim](#stmt-prop-estimates-energy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-estimates-energy): Construct harmonic product-rule backgrounds; combine the local integrated Dirac inequality with the cylinder gradient identity and flux-minimizing tube comparison. -> Uniform retained-region bounds force reduced spherical flux to vanish in the small-width region.
- **step-metric-clamp-choices** [claim](#stmt-thm-estimates-clamp) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-estimates-choices): Prove the isolated period inequality, transfer the vertex test to finite sizes, and separate fixed old-cap constants from problem-dependent isolation thresholds. -> Simultaneous reduced-class inequalities and an explicit noncircular order of finite choices.
- **step-index-and-loss-accounting** [claim](#stmt-lem-indices-virtual-sums) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-indices-virtual-sums): Compute closed and lens indices using sharp reference fillings; eliminate cap spinors and allocate all losses once in the virtual decomposition. -> Conserved virtual dimensions and exact particle and lens penalties.
- **step-numerical-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-thm-indices-exclusion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-indices-exclusion): Apply the clamp square estimate, distinct-unit incidence assignments, fixed-run and reducer-run bounds, and outside exceptional evaluations to the virtual dimension identities. -> Conditional on admissibility, only legitimate instantons and clean minimum trace lens ends survive.
- **step-exact-analytic-library** [claim](#stmt-prop-analysis-ordinary-library) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-analysis-ordinary-library): Modify zero-winding sweeps, segment them at primary faces, and construct finite detecting samples and compactly supported equivariant outputs. -> An independently available ordinary exact-support perturbation and representative library.
- **step-analytic-compactness-and-candidates** [claim](#stmt-lem-analysis-finite-data) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-analysis-finite-data): Prove compatible implicit charts, energy nonconcentration, removable particles, true-neck decay, exact incidence persistence, and finite candidate degeneration ranges. -> Compactness and field-independence needed to regularize candidate projections.
- **step-fixed-regularity-and-links** [claim](#stmt-prop-analysis-instanton-link) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-analysis-instanton-link): Regularize fixed-type equations componentwise, make the legitimate instanton Dirac operators surjective, and install quadratic phase sections on their projective links. -> Fixed-type exclusion and regular oriented instanton-link collars with the stated multiplicity.
- **step-mixed-finite-regularization** [claim](#stmt-prop-analysis-finite-induction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-analysis-finite-induction): Project away zero-spinor reducers and regularize compact candidate images in finite degeneration order, preserving paired lens exteriors and instanton collars. -> Forbidden mixed candidates are absent and the surviving trace-main problems are regular and isolated.
- **step-minimum-cap-and-weight-blocks** [claim](#stmt-lem-gluing-triangular) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-gluing-triangular): Regularize the framed harmonic cap crossing, retain its scalar obstruction, change its weight, and eliminate shared parameter derivatives by a triangular correction. -> Invertible limiting main and cap blocks suitable for finite-neck gluing.
- **step-exhaustive-lens-gluing** [claim](#stmt-prop-gluing-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-gluing-collar): Construct an asymmetric-weight finite-neck inverse, solve by contraction, and improve converging half-solutions to exponential closeness for exhaustion. -> Every surviving lens end has an exhaustive regular collar with unchanged branch weights.
- **step-complete-weighted-count** [claim](#stmt-thm-analysis-regularization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-gluing-collar-2): Regularize the free interior relative to the constructed collars and apply the compatible finite-branch boundary rule. -> A compact oriented weighted free count with precisely the proved instanton and lens ends.
- **step-orientations-and-contradiction** [claim](#stmt-thm-gluing-contradiction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-gluing-contradiction): Transport the ordinary local cap sign through the complex Dirac determinant, pair lens-bit ends branchwise, and apply the weighted boundary identity. -> The boundary identity contradicts the nonzero ordinary count under the remaining cosmetic identification.
- **step-main-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-gluing-contradiction-2): Combine the remaining-case contradiction with the preliminary meridional, homological, and slope reductions. -> The stated orientation-preserving filling equivalence forces equal slopes.

          "anchor": "stmt-thm-ordinary-units",
          "exact_quote": "Let $C(Y_j;\\mathbb Z)$ be the irreducible, unframed instanton complex with the determinants just specified. Compatible small perturbations and coherent orientations can be chosen so that the rigid counts define integral chain maps, and the rigid and interval counts have the following properties over $\\mathbb F_2$.*\n\n1.  *Each rigid meridional handle map $Y_r\\longrightarrow Y_{r+1}$, for $r=0,1$, is a unit whenever its determinant has the specified end restrictions. The rigid count on their composite is their composition up to chain homotopy. Denote this composite by $f_+:C(Y_0)\\longrightarrow C(Y_2)$.*\n\n2.  *On the path $2\\longrightarrow\\infty\\longrightarrow0$, let $F_l,A$ be the capped Seifert classes of squares $-2,0$, respectively, with $F_l\\cdot A=0$, and let $S_l=A-F_l$. Choose the base determinant $c(F_l,A)=(0,1)$ and the two determinants $c+e\\operatorname{PD}(S_l)$, $e=0,1$, identified off $S_l$. The sum modulo two of the interval counts of actual index $-1$ is a unit $g_+:C(Y_2;\\mathbb F_2)\\longrightarrow C(Y_0;\\mathbb F_2)$.*\n\n3.  *The mirror construction, read backwards, gives units $f_-:C(Y_{-2})\\longrightarrow C(Y_0)$ on the rigid path through $-1$, and $g_-:C(Y_0;\\mathbb F_2)\\longrightarrow C(Y_{-2};\\mathbb F_2)$ on $0\\longrightarrow\\infty\\longrightarrow-2$. For $g_-$ the base evaluations are $(1,0)$ and the second determinant differs by the Poincaré dual of the intervening $(-2)$-sphere.*\n\n*For the summed interval maps, each summand has an integral orientation; the assertion that the sum is a chain map and a unit is required only after reduction modulo two. End identifications, including any tensor automorphisms, are fixed before composing the maps.",

          "exact_quote": "For every fixed derivative order $k$, the metric near an edge with shrink parameter $\\delta=r_i$ or $h_i$ has the following description. There is a homogeneous radius $R$ and a cone metric $g_{\\mathrm c}$ such that, in scale-invariant $C^k$ norms on every dyadic annulus, $$\\|g-g_{\\mathrm c}\\|_{C^k(g_{\\mathrm c})}\n \\le C_k\\bigl(\\delta/R^2+R^2\\bigr),\n \\qquad C\\sqrt\\delta\\le R\\le R_*.\n \\label{eq:geometry:cone-error}$$ The estimates include smooth toric axes and are uniform on the $L\\to\\infty$ tips. In affine moment coordinates $\\mu_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ centered at the relevant homogeneous cone vertex, the scale $\\mu_{\\mathrm{loc}}=\\delta\\widehat\\mu_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ gives $g=\\delta(g_{\\mathrm{sat}}+o(1))$ on compact sets away from any remaining cone point. The metric $g_{\\mathrm{sat}}$ is a three-direction Hessian metric with strictly positive scalar curvature on those compact sets.*\n\n*There are conformal changes making all the necessary annuli asymptotically cylindrical, with fixed positive limiting link sizes. They have nonnegative scalar curvature and preserve strict positivity on smooth compact regions.
